questions.q: What does Stein call the most important first step toward success?
a: Knowing yourself through honest introspection
Surrounding yourself with expert mentors
Studying the habits of champions
Setting a strict daily schedule
questions.why: Lesson 1 says self-awareness gives you a starting point, much like a map needs your location.

questions.q: What does comparison ultimately produce, according to the summary?
a: Self-doubt and wasted time
Sharper goals and faster progress
A stronger sense of gratitude
Better relationships with peers
questions.why: Lesson 2 calls comparison the mother of doubt and says it drains time and energy.

questions.q: Why is comparing yourself with others useless, according to the summary?
a: It never turns you into the person you admire
Other people always hide their struggles
Comparison only works among close friends
Everyone improves at exactly the same rate
questions.why: Lesson 2 says comparison cannot make you the subject of your envy, so it adds no benefit.

questions.q: How does the summary suggest approaching a large goal?
a: Start small and build up through gradual steps
Wait for the perfect moment to begin
Work in long bursts without any breaks
Focus only on the final result
questions.why: Lesson 3 recommends small, repeatable steps instead of facing the whole mountain at once.

questions.q: Which example shows how to make a big task feel manageable?
a: Doing ten abs ten times rather than one hundred at once
Running a marathon without any training
Lifting the heaviest weight on day one
Skipping the first week of a new routine
questions.why: Lesson 3 uses that exercise example to show how smaller units make a goal less daunting.
